rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reads mustaqarr and mustawdaʿ either as verbal nouns meaning settlement and deposit, or as place nouns meaning where settling and depositing occur.
rows.anchor: “Müstekar” ve “müstevda‘” istikrar ve istîdâ‘mânasına masdar-ı mîmî veya mahall-i istikrar ve mahall-i istîdâ‘mânasına ism-i mekân olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms encompass alternating human stages from loins through womb and worldly life to the grave, and differing conditions such as settled or traveling, male or female, and living or dead.
rows.anchor: Sulbden rahime, rahimden dünyaya, dünyadan kabre kâh istikrar kâh istîdâ‘iki mütenâvib hâl içindesiniz

rows.speaker: İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ya‘kūb’dan Revh
rows.claim: In the readings of Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Rawh from Yaqub, mustaqarr has kasra on kāf and is an active participle; mustawdaʿ is passive.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ya‘kūb’dan Revh kıraatlerinde kāfın kesriyle ism-i fâ‘il olarak فَمُسْتَقَرٌّۭ okunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, some are settled while others remain deposited: in loins or womb, created in actuality or still potential, mature or under guardianship, resident or traveling, and alive or dead.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bu kıraate göre mâna: Hepiniz bir nefisten inşâ edilmiş olduğunuz hâlde kiminiz müstekır bulunuyor, istikrar hâlinde, kiminiz de henüz vedî‘a hâlinde;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature's regularity cannot by itself explain the actual emergence of many differing branches from one source; the real originating cause is the Creator.
rows.anchor: Demek ki illet-i vâkı‘a, madde ve tabî‘at-ı menşe’ değil hâlıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every event added to matter and its originating nature involves a new act of creation.
rows.anchor: Maddeye ve tabî‘at-ı menşe’e inzimam eden her hâdisede bir halk-ı cedîd vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation brings forth novelty while also proportioning it to prior creation and developing and increasing it through divine craft.
rows.anchor: bu îcâdı îcâd-ı sâbıka tevfik ve rabt ederek onu tenmiye ve tezyid eden bir takdir ve bir sun‘-i bedî‘vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Change, emergence, and difference testify to creation, while stability, regularity, correspondence, and order testify to divine craftsmanship.
rows.anchor: her istikrar, her ıttırad, her tevafuk, her nizam bir delîl-i san‘attır.

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some object that creating from nonbeing conflicts with the continued existence of causes and the multiplication of effects.
rows.anchor: Bazıları ‘ademden halkı bekā-yı illet ve tezâyüf-i illiyet kāidesine muhalif zannederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That objection applies if nonbeing is treated as a cause; when the Creator is the cause, neither causal continuity nor the principle of causation is violated.
rows.anchor: Fakat halkta illet hâlık olmak üzere mülâhaza edildiği zaman ne bekā-yı illet ne de tezâyüf-i illiyet hiçbiri tehâlüf etmemiş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causation means every effect depends on its cause, not that the effect equals the cause in power; a true cause creates its effect rather than being depleted by giving it something of itself.
rows.anchor: ma‘lûlün behemehâl illetine müsâvâtı mânasına telakkī edilmemelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seed and tree or parent and child are not ultimate causes and effects; they are means and places where origination is deposited.
rows.anchor: Tohum ve ağaç, baba ve evlâd, usûl ve fürû‘yekdiğerinin illet ve ma‘lûlü değil, sebeb ve müsebbebi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs of creative power become more apparent as one moves from minerals to plants, animals, and humans, whose complex diversity makes their signs especially abundant.
rows.anchor: cemâdât ve me‘âdîn üzerindeki ma‘nâ-yı halk nebâtâta, hayvânâta doğru geçildikçe bir nisbet-i mütezâyide ile artar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diversity of human conditions across successive generations shows that God creates every detail of each kind of emergence, not only its first source.
rows.anchor: tenasül kanununun iş‘âr ettiği kesret-i tenevvü‘ve tehavvül kat‘iyyetle isbat eder ki Allah teâlâ yalnız menşe’lerin hâlıkı değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı presents settled and deposited states as a concise, scientifically comprehensive maxim that lays out the proofs contained in the surrounding signs.
rows.anchor: bütün bu delâili ve âyâtın vücûh-i delâletlerini bütün vuzûh ve tenkīh-i ilmîsiyle gösteren bir düsturdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's detailed signs are addressed to people with subtle, deep understanding in themselves, the class of discerning sages.
rows.anchor: Biz bu âyetleri ehl-i fıkıh olan, nefsinde ince ve derin bir fehmi bulunan zümre-i hükemâ için tafsil ettik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiqh originally means understanding something through its causes and wisdom with fine discernment, and it includes self-knowledge.
rows.anchor: “fıkıh” asl-ı lügatta bir şeyi ilel ü hikmetiyle anlamak, fehm-i dakīk ile fehm etmek mânasınadır ki bunda ma‘rifetü’n-nefs mânası da mündericdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of the outward signs is reached through inward signs, and sound judgment comes from their correspondence; without understanding human life, knowledge of the wider world remains insecure.
rows.anchor: âyât-ı âfâkiye, âyât-ı enfüsiye ile bilinir ve karâr-ı hak ikisinin intibâkından verilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because human emergence is more complex than plant and animal emergence, self-knowledge is harder and is necessary for sound study of the world.
rows.anchor: neş’et-i insâniye ise neş’et-i nebâtiye ve hayvâniyeden daha cem‘iyyetli olduğu için ma‘rifet-i nefs daha mu‘dil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The move from the audience who know to those who understand narrows the audience: analyzing these details requires more than ordinary learning, namely insight into the self.
rows.anchor: evvelkinde لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ ile iktifâ olunduğu hâlde burada لِقَوْمٍۢ يَفْقَهُونَ buyurularak daha ziyade tahsis kılınmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without inward discernment, further detail is useless; for those who have it, this verse is the key to examining the details, and such people themselves are among its detailed signs.
rows.anchor: fakīhü’n-nefs olmayanlar için ne kadar tafsîlât verilse boştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same principle unfolds the splitting of grain and seeds, the sequence of purification and development, and rejects treating the elements as an effective first cause.
rows.anchor: aynı düstur dâhilinde فَالِقُ ٱلْحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰ mazmununu teşrih ve silsile-i ıstıfâ ve tekâmülü tavzih

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends down water and brings forth the vegetation of every thing, activating growth and development in plants and in things nourished or transformed through plant life.
rows.anchor: Habb ü nevâtın ve her türlü nebâtın ve insanlar ve hayvanlar gibi nebat ile tegaddî eden veya me‘âdin vesâire gibi nebâtâta gıda olarak onlara tehavvül ve temessül edecek olan her şeyin nebâtiyetini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the plant or thing God brings forth fresh green growth, from which stacked grains emerge.
rows.anchor: ve binâen‘aleyh ondan, o nebattan veya o şeyden taze bir yeşillik, bir çim çıkardık.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close-packed grain ears resemble cavalry companies lined for battle, their spears extended against an attack from the air.
rows.anchor: mızraklarını uzatmış süvari bölükleri gibi ne güzel müterâkibdirler

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌۭ دَانِيَةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Date palms produce nearby hanging clusters from their spathes; the verse also names grape gardens, olives, and pomegranates.
rows.anchor: yani tomurcuğundan da {قِنْوَانٌۭ دَانِيَةٌۭ} yakınlara sarkmış salkımlar olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruits' likeness and difference restate more plainly the rule of regularity and variation signaled earlier by settled and deposited states.
rows.anchor: Bu müşabehet ve ‘adem-i müşabehet kaydı, yukarıda istikrar ve istîda‘ile ifade olunan

words: ٱنظُرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ وَيَنْعِهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compare a fruit when it first appears, still unripe, with its maturity: their difference displays nurture and a clear course of development, signs for believers of God's existence, unity, power, and providential wisdom.
rows.anchor: Arada ne büyük bir fark vardır, ve bu farkta ne mühim bir feyz-i terbiye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water's descent and greenery's emergence are past tense, while producing stacked grains is present or future and portrays their potential; buds and clusters are coordinated similarly.
rows.anchor: Suyun inzâli, nebâtın, çimin ihrâcı فَأَخْرَجْنَا / أَنزَلَ diye mâzî sîgasıyla ifade edilmiş olduğu hâlde, habb-i müterâkibi ihraç نُّخْرِجُ diye istikbal sîgasıyla

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌۭ دَانِيَةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tense and growth imagery also hints that Islam at the verse's Meccan revelation was like grass or a bud, while the Quran was heavenly mercy and believers' future would resemble mature gardens and fruit.
rows.anchor: dîn-i İslâm’ın henüz o çim, o tomurcuk misâlinde olduğuna, Kur’ân’ın semâdan inen bir rahmet bulunduğuna ve mü’minlerin istikbâli o cennetler ve kemâle ermiş meyveler gibi olacağına bir işaret dahi edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi explains the order: staple grain precedes tree fruits because food comes before delicacies; date palms then precede other fruits because dates are Arab staple food and philosophers see many animal-like qualities in the palm.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Burada evvelâ hubûbat, sonra nahl, ineb, zeytin, rummân dört nevi ağaç zikredilmiş ve zer‘, eşcâra takdim olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to call the palm the maternal aunt of the community and say it was created from what remained of Adam's clay.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm da demiştir ki ‘Ammeniz, yani halanız nahleye ikram ediniz. Çünkü o Âdem’in tînetinin bakiyesinden halk edildi’

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi calls grapes the noblest fruit and describes their usefulness from the first shoots and leaves through unripe and ripe fruit, including storage on the vine.
rows.anchor: Zira üzüm envâ‘-i fevâkihin en şereflisidir.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi lists four products obtained from grapes: raisins, grape molasses, vinegar, and wine, and says their benefits would fill volumes.
rows.anchor: Sonra üzümden tenavül olunacak dört nevi şey yapılır: Kuru üzüm, pekmez, sirke, şarap.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Although wine is forbidden by Islamic law, Razi cites the Quran's judgment that its sin outweighs its benefit.
rows.anchor: Gerçi şarabı şeriat tahrim etmiştir.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says grape seeds are especially valuable and that physicians prepare remedies from them for weak, damp stomachs; contemporary doctors agree when seeds are chewed and crushed.
rows.anchor: tertibler[^16] yaparlar ki zayıf ve râtib mideler için pek büyük menfaatleri olur.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi concludes that grapes deserve the title “sultan of fruits.”
rows.anchor: Hâsılı üzüm “sultânü’lfevâkih” ıtlâkına şâyân bir meyvedir.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi notes that olives are eaten and their oil has extensive benefits and uses in food and other matters.
rows.anchor: dânesi tenâvül olunur, yağının da yemek vesâir husûsâtta ne kadar menfa‘ati azîm ve isti‘mâli kesîr olduğu mâlumdur.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi describes pomegranate as rind, membranes, seeds, and juice: its first three parts are powerfully cold, dry, dense, and astringent, while its tasty, delicate juice is nearer to balance, suits balanced constitutions, strengthens weak ones, and acts as both food and medicine.
rows.anchor: ilk üçü yani kışrı, şahmı, çekirdeği bârid, yâbis, kesif, kābızdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı takes pomegranate's contrasting dense parts and delicate juice as a clear example of the verse's rule that likeness and difference coexist.
rows.anchor: Yani bunda مُشْتَبِهًۭا وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍ mazmûnundaki tevâfuk ve tegāyür kanununun bâriz bir misâli vardır.
